newsitem.title: UK: Human "mad cow" cases number 21 in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Human "mad cow" cases number 21 in Britain.

text.p: The British government said on Monday that 21 people -- an increase of two since last month -- had been struck down by a new variety of brain illness linked with mad cow disease
Last month the government reported 19 suspected and confirmed cases of the new variant of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD).
The Edinburgh-based CJD surveillance unit reports every suspected case of the brain-wasting disease, which usually affects about one in a million people.

The new strain, identified in 1996, hits at a much younger age than CJD usually does and scientists still do not know if there will be an epidemic to mirror the epidemic of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE or mad cow disease) that hit British herds in the 1980s.
Experts say BSE will die out early in the next century. They believe it was caused by feeding cattle the rendered remains of sheep infected with scrapie, a closely related disease.
Any animal parts that might be infectious are now banned from use at all but scientists confirm that people may have eaten infected beef parts in the 1980s.
The unit said there were three cases of the new variety of CJD in 1995, 10 in 1996 and eight so far this year.
